newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Carter calls on Sudan to forge peace with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Carter calls on Sudan to forge peace with rebels.

text.p: Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter said on Monday that the Islamist government in Khartoum would have to forge peace with rebels and neighbours for Sudan's civil strife to end.

"The only way through which peace would come to Sudan is when the Khartoum government could reach full agreement both with the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) as well as the leaders of the neighbouring countries," Carter said in Addis Ababa.
"Until that happens I do not think the conflict inside Sudan is going to stop."

Carter, who said he was visiting the region to explore new possibilites for renewed peace talks, hoped that member states of the Inter-Governmental Authority for Development (IGAD) would convene talks to bring peace to Sudan.
He said a peace deal that was signed on Monday between splinter southern Sudan rebel groups and the Khartoum government has "some positive aspects".
He said however without the participation of the SPLA and the political opposition comprehensive peace in Sudan was unthinkable.

"Everyone understands that additional detailed negotiations will have to be conducted to reach a comprehnsive agreement on peace between Khartoum, SPLA , the democratic alliance and the leaders of the neighbouring states," he said.

Carter said he thought that Monday's peace deal indicated a willingness by Khartoum to acknowledge that all Sudanese should be treated equally and have the right to their own religion and ethnic status.
"These are recent developments which I have not heard of during my numerous visits to Sudan," he added.
Carter said he had talks with Ethiopian Prime Minister Meles Zenawi concering Sudan, but refused to give details.
He said he also met Sudan's enovy to the United Nations who is in Addis Ababa with a message from the Sudanese leadership to Meles. He refused to discuss the nature of the message.

Carter, who flies home on Monday night, did not mention a claim by Sudanese rebels that a government warplane bombed a southern town on Sunday, preventing him from landing there to meet a rebel leader.
